03 · Model architecture

One contract, five implementations

Every model takes a (batch, 30, n_features) sequence and outputs a single scalar — predicted RUL. Four PyTorch architectures share this input/output contract; a Random Forest sits alongside them as a non-deep-learning benchmark, not part of the modeling approach. Select a layer to read its tensor shape transformation.

Flattens the whole window into one vector, ignores time order entirely — the simplest baseline.

↓ ↓ ↓ ↓ ↓

MLPModel cell 29 ↗
1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 91011 
class MLPModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, window_size, n_features, hidden=128):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Flatten(),
            nn.Linear(window_size * n_features, hidden), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden, hidden // 2), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden // 2, 1),
        )
    def forward(self, x):
        return self.net(x).squeeze(1)

Slides learnable filters along the time axis to pick up short local degradation trends.

↓ ↓ ↓ ↓ ↓
Tensor shape [B, 30, F]
1D-CNNModel cell 29 ↗
1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 910111213 
class CNN1DModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, n_features, hidden=64):
        super().__init__()
        self.conv = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv1d(n_features, hidden, kernel_size=3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv1d(hidden, hidden, kernel_size=3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.AdaptiveAvgPool1d(1),
        )
        self.head = nn.Linear(hidden, 1)
    def forward(self, x):
        x = x.permute(0, 2, 1)   # (B, window, features) -> (B, features, window)
        x = self.conv(x).squeeze(-1)
        return self.head(x).squeeze(1)

Reads the window one cycle at a time, keeping a memory cell that can retain long-range information.

Tensor shape [B, 30, F]
LSTMModel cell 29 ↗
12345678 
class LSTMModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, n_features, hidden=64):
        super().__init__()
        self.lstm = nn.LSTM(n_features, hidden, batch_first=True)
        self.head = nn.Linear(hidden, 1)
    def forward(self, x):
        _, (h_n, _) = self.lstm(x)   # h_n: (1, B, hidden)
        return self.head(h_n[-1]).squeeze(1)

Same recurrent idea as LSTM with simpler gating — fewer parameters, typically faster to train.

↓ ↓ ↓

class GRUModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, n_features, hidden=64):
        super().__init__()
        self.gru = nn.GRU(n_features, hidden, batch_first=True)
        self.head = nn.Linear(hidden, 1)
    def forward(self, x):
        _, h_n = self.gru(x)
        return self.head(h_n[-1]).squeeze(1)

Ensemble of decision trees on the flattened window — a sanity check for whether the extra complexity of a neural net is actually earning its keep. Not part of the modeling approach; used strictly as a non-deep-learning benchmark.
